turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start by telling me who decided that, and when.
Sorry, I'm a bit frazzled, it's report card week.
Report card week isn't Owen's problem, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
You're the first parent this month who's actually listened to me. Thank you. I mean it.
Don't manage me, Hale. I'm still waiting for an answer: who entered that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
I really needed that today. Can we just be kind to each other in here?
Kindness would have been a phone call before that mark went in. Who decided, Hale, and on what basis?
